paragraphs: Transformers use rotary position embeddings to represent where tokens occur. Standard implementations give every attention head the same rotation frequencies and scaling, even though different heads can serve different functions. This paper investigates that mismatch through simplified retrieval tasks and tests of generalization to longer sequences, combining theoretical arguments with empirical evidence.

AdaRoPE gives each attention head learnable rotation frequencies and attention scaling factors. These choices let positional encoding adapt to the head’s role instead of imposing one shared schedule. The authors argue that uniform settings can waste embedding capacity and weaken performance, especially with long contexts. They also extend this reasoning to context extension, where changing all heads identically can be suboptimal.

The evaluated pretrained language models consistently outperform the compared RoPE variants, including partial RoPE and a baseline without positional embeddings. Head-specific scaling also improves context extension while better retaining short-context performance, both through extrapolation and continued training on long contexts. The findings support treating positional encoding as a component that should adapt within individual attention heads.
icml-2026-adarope-not-all-attention-head.tldr: AdaRoPE learns positional rotation and scaling separately for each attention head, improving the evaluated models’ context handling.

paragraphs: Training an agent to complete an interactive task requires learning across a sequence of decisions. Agentic reinforcement learning has shown promise for this setting, but its training can become unstable or collapse. That instability makes it harder to scale to larger environments and longer interactions, and also makes comparisons between algorithmic choices less dependable.

ARLArena provides a standardized testbed and a training recipe for studying these issues under controlled, reproducible conditions. The researchers separate policy-gradient design into four core dimensions and examine how choices along each dimension affect performance and stability. This turns a broad training problem into a more structured investigation of which decisions contribute to failure.

The analysis leads to SAMPO, a policy optimization method designed to address the dominant instability sources identified by the framework. Across the evaluated agentic tasks, SAMPO maintains consistently stable training and strong performance. The contribution therefore includes both a method for training agents and a systematic way to investigate stability, making algorithmic design choices easier to assess.
icml-2026-arlarena-a-unified-framework-f.tldr: ARLArena systematically studies agent-training instability and uses the findings to develop SAMPO, which trains stably across the evaluated tasks.

paragraphs: Steganography hides messages inside seemingly ordinary content. In diffusion image generation, a message can be embedded in the initial noise, but denoising and subsequent image decoding weaken that signal. This creates a trade-off between how much information is embedded and how reliably it can be recovered. The paper links extraction accuracy to the separation between images representing different message hypotheses.

ASIR addresses both signal placement and recovery without additional training. Antipodal Sampling maximizes separation in probability space, making competing message possibilities easier to distinguish. Iterative Recovery then treats extraction as a gradient-based optimization problem that works to reverse nonlinear distortions introduced during generation. The framework applies to diffusion models operating directly in pixels and those operating in latent representations.

The authors describe ASIR as provably secure and report leading experimental performance. Their results include embedding up to 65,536 bits in pixel-space models and 16,384 bits in latent-space models with 99% recovery accuracy. Embedded messages also remain statistically undetectable to the deep steganalyzers evaluated. These findings connect improved signal separation and active recovery with higher practical message capacity.
icml-2026-asir-steganography-for-diffusi.tldr: ASIR combines separated message encodings with optimization-based extraction to improve hidden-message capacity and recovery in diffusion-generated images.

paragraphs: Using language models to improve advertising creatives changes an auction’s economics because generating those improvements costs computation. The platform must decide how much to invest in ad quality while advertisers’ automated bidding agents respond under budget constraints. The paper models this interaction as a dynamic leader–follower game, with the platform choosing investments and bidders reacting.

The proposed Platform-Investment Mechanism explicitly incorporates inference costs into the platform’s decisions. For bidders, an online dual-descent algorithm with regularization learns bidding strategies as the environment changes. For the platform, the researchers formulate investment as a continuous control problem and develop a two-timescale learning algorithm based on proximal policy optimization. This connects creative enhancement, its cost, and bidding behavior within one framework.

The platform algorithm is proved to converge to a Stackelberg stationary point, a qualified convergence result rather than a claim of global optimality. Experiments using large real-world datasets and contemporary language models report significant improvements over heuristic baselines in revenue, social welfare, and user engagement. The findings indicate that coordinating investment and bidding can improve several auction outcomes together.
icml-2026-autobidding-auctions-with-llm-.tldr: The paper jointly models costly LLM creative enhancement and automated bidding, improving auction outcomes over tested heuristic approaches.

paragraphs: Audio-visual speaker tracking combines sound and video to locate active speakers and follow them over time. Existing datasets often contain simple, uniform scenes and coarse annotations. As a result, a method can look successful by associating visible people with simultaneous audio, without being thoroughly tested on movement, interruptions in visibility, or more demanding reasoning across the two signals.

AVTrack introduces a dataset for human-centered audio-visual instance segmentation in dynamic real-world scenes. Its challenging conditions include camera movement, people becoming visually occluded, and changes in position. These situations make the benchmark more demanding because identifying the speaker requires maintaining an understanding of people and their locations as the scene changes.

Representative methods suffer substantial performance drops when evaluated on AVTrack. The result exposes a gap between performance in simpler settings and robust tracking in complex scenes. The researchers also provide a simple baseline to support further work. The main contribution is therefore an evaluation resource that makes weaknesses in temporal modeling and audio-visual reasoning easier to reveal and study.
icml-2026-avtrack-audio-visual-tracking-.tldr: AVTrack tests audio-visual speaker tracking in dynamic scenes and reveals substantial performance drops in representative existing methods.

paragraphs: Graph out-of-distribution detection identifies entire graphs that differ from the typical graphs in a dataset. Earlier approaches often emphasize the connections inside each graph. CLINIC also examines relationships among graph samples, seeking semantic structure in groups of samples that are close in a learned representation. This supplies context beyond each graph’s own topology.

The method first builds a contextual affinity graph describing those relationships in hidden space. A meta-graph neural network then captures higher-order affinity to improve its understanding of the structure. Twin concordance learning encourages agreement in two ways: affinity distributions should align across different views, and contextually similar neighbors should have consistent representations. Together, these objectives aim to make graph representations more discriminative and robust.

CLINIC also introduces a compression strategy intended to expand the decision boundary and improve separation between familiar and anomalous graphs. Experiments across ten real datasets show better performance than the compared baselines. The reported findings support using relationships between graph samples alongside internal graph structure when learning to recognize unusual graphs.
icml-2026-clinic-towards-high-quality-gr.tldr: CLINIC improves graph anomaly detection by learning contextual relationships among graph samples and enforcing consistency across views and neighbors.

paragraphs: A pretrained video generator can become a controllable world model by learning latent actions that influence what happens next. Common approaches train the latent action model and the world model separately. That separation creates redundant training and limits how much the two components can adapt to each other. Training them jointly is appealing, but can cause their representations to collapse.

CoLA-World enables joint learning through a warm-up phase that aligns a newly initialized latent action model with the pretrained world model. After this alignment, the world model’s learning signals help shape the latent action representation. In the other direction, the improving action model gives the world model a more precise and adaptable control interface. Each component can therefore guide the other’s development.

In the reported experiments, CoLA-World matches or exceeds prior two-stage approaches in video simulation quality and downstream visual planning. These findings suggest that carefully preparing the components for joint training can make their interaction productive. The warm-up is central to the approach because it addresses the representational mismatch that makes direct joint training difficult.
icml-2026-co-evolving-latent-action-worl.tldr: CoLA-World uses an alignment warm-up to jointly train latent actions and a pretrained world model, matching or improving on tested two-stage methods.

paragraphs: Continual multimodal learning asks a model to acquire new tasks sequentially while retaining previous abilities. Mixture-of-experts architectures offer specialized components, but adding experts indiscriminately increases model size quickly. Changing shared routing components can also cause forgetting by disrupting how previously learned knowledge is accessed. CoPE addresses both problems without replaying data from earlier tasks.

Its probe-guided extension mechanism determines when and where additional experts are needed. This makes expansion responsive to task complexity and aims to limit unnecessary parameter growth. At inference time, a probabilistic task locator selects suitable task-specific components without requiring an explicit task label. It uses a variational autoencoder reconstruction strategy to match input distributions to the appropriate router.

The design connects selective growth with automatic routing: preserving expertise is useful only if the model can still send an input to the right components. On the CoIN benchmark’s eight visual question-answering tasks, CoPE reports strong continual learning performance with a compact model, substantially less forgetting, and lower parameter overhead than prior methods. These results support adaptive expansion as a practical approach to sequential task learning.
icml-2026-cope-continual-probe-guided-ex.tldr: CoPE selectively adds experts and automatically routes inputs to reduce forgetting and model growth during continual multimodal learning.

paragraphs: Embodied agents must explore environments where observations are complex and actions produce complicated changes. Measuring exploration in a learned latent representation can help, but that representation may be noisy or change as the policy changes. Exploration objectives based on random goals or fixed directions can then become brittle and fail to expand overall coverage.

Covariance Volume Maximization addresses representation stability and exploration incentives together. First, it learns a behavioral state encoder with a policy-mixture objective, reducing representation drift as exploration policies change. Second, each transition receives a reward equal to its increase in the log-determinant of the covariance of recent latent displacements. This measures expansion across directions and favors changes in directions that have received less coverage.

The objective coincides with the classical D-optimal design criterion, supplying an information-efficiency interpretation of the exploration reward. Experiments on embodied navigation and manipulation report substantially better exploration efficiency and robustness, with effective scaling across environments. The findings support combining a stable behavioral representation with an explicit measure of multidirectional coverage, rather than relying only on individually novel movements.
icml-2026-covariance-volume-maximization.tldr: CVM rewards expansion into underexplored latent directions while stabilizing the representation used to measure exploration.

paragraphs: Multi-view graph clustering groups nodes using several views of graph information. Existing methods can depend too heavily on fixed local connections and combine views too simply. APGC addresses these issues by modifying which relationships the model relies on and adapting how much information it takes from different nodes and views.

Its structural refinement module uses attribute similarity to strengthen useful connections and suppress relationships whose semantics conflict. Incorporating global attribute information promotes links between similar nodes, helping the graph neural network learn representations that distinguish clusters. The refinement is bidirectional in the sense that it can both reinforce and weaken connections, rather than merely adding more structure.

A second module uses reliable pseudo-labels to guide weighted fusion at both the node level and the view level. This allows different information sources to contribute unequally where appropriate. Experiments on six datasets, including graphs that connect similar nodes and graphs that connect dissimilar nodes, show superior clustering performance. The results support jointly refining graph structure and learning how to combine multiple views.
icml-2026-deep-multi-view-graph-clusteri.tldr: APGC improves multi-view graph clustering by refining connections using attributes and adaptively combining information with pseudo-label guidance.

paragraphs: This paper investigates the internal mechanisms behind emotional expression in language-model outputs. Its questions concern whether emotional representations persist across contexts, which model components implement them, and whether those components can control generated emotion. The study’s evidence addresses expression and internal computation; its title’s reference to feeling does not establish subjective emotional experience.

The researchers build a controlled Scenario–Event with Valence dataset to compare internal states across emotions. They extract emotion directions that remain consistent across contexts, then use analytical decomposition and causal analysis to identify relevant neurons and attention heads. Removing or enhancing these components tests their causal roles, going beyond simply observing correlations between activations and emotional text.

The authors also measure each sublayer’s influence on the final emotion representation and assemble the local components into global emotion circuits. Direct intervention on those circuits achieves 99.65% emotion-expression accuracy on the test set, exceeding prompting and steering methods in the reported comparison. The findings link interpretable internal components to a concrete means of controlling emotional expression.
icml-2026-do-llms-feel-emotion-circuits-.tldr: The study identifies and causally tests language-model emotion circuits, then uses them to control emotional expression with high test-set accuracy.

paragraphs: Existing LoRA adaptations can lose their intended style or damage generated structure when transferred directly to distilled video diffusion models. The paper studies this incompatibility in the models’ weights. Its focus is on variants produced through step distillation or causal distillation, where a mismatch in weight space can prevent an otherwise useful adaptation from functioning properly.

The analysis identifies spectral interference within shared functional clusters defined over singular subspaces. In plain terms, the adaptation and the distilled model can rely on overlapping weight-space directions while routing information through them differently. Their contributions may reinforce one another excessively or cancel one another. The authors describe these conflicting pathways as the source of incompatibility despite shared spectral rigidity.

Cluster-Aware Spectral Arbitration, or CASA, uses spectral density to balance preserving the target model’s structure against restoring alignment with the LoRA. It performs this arbitration without data. Experiments show that CASA reduces artifacts and restores LoRA functionality. The contribution combines an explanation of transfer failures with a weight-space procedure designed to resolve the identified interference.
icml-2026-exploring-data-free-lora-trans.tldr: CASA uses data-free spectral arbitration to reduce interference when transferring LoRAs to distilled video diffusion models.

paragraphs: Distributional learning compares probability distributions using objectives such as optimal transport or Sinkhorn divergence. Yet optimization commonly uses ordinary Euclidean steps in parameter space. This paper argues that the geometry of those steps can be structurally mismatched with the geometry of the objective. It defines a local condition number, called geometry-misalignment, to quantify that distortion.

For a broad class of problems, the authors prove that Euclidean first-order methods face a slowdown proportional to misalignment, even when the objective has strong convexity and smoothness in its intrinsic geometry. Geometry-aware preconditioned methods achieve matching upper bounds that do not depend on misalignment. The analysis also connects this issue to statistical efficiency: with finite optimization budgets, misalignment contributes an optimization-dependent excess-risk term.

The proposed framework estimates misalignment and selectively enables geometry-aware updates when needed. Experiments on distribution matching for domain adaptation support the theory, with improvements concentrated in highly misaligned cases and negligible overhead. The practical implication is that optimization effort can be directed toward correcting geometry where the mismatch actually impedes learning.
icml-2026-geometry-misalignment-in-distr.tldr: The paper quantifies geometry-induced optimization slowdowns and develops selective geometry-aware updates that improve highly misaligned distribution-learning problems.

paragraphs: Hierarchical decision making divides a difficult control problem into high-level goals and lower-level decisions. Reinforcement learning can struggle to enforce strict constraints, while optimal-control formulations can be shortsighted or computationally expensive. Combining the two is promising, but the lower-level optimization problem is often designed using heuristics that may not align with the overall task.

This paper uses inverse optimization to learn the structure of that lower-level problem from expert demonstrations. Instead of specifying its objective only through manual design, the framework uses demonstrated decisions to inform how the structured policy should optimize. The purpose is to connect upper-level goal abstraction with lower-level choices that remain aligned with long-term task goals.

The researchers evaluate the framework on network resource allocation and continuous collision avoidance, covering distinct kinds of decisions. It consistently outperforms the tested end-to-end reinforcement learning, learning-augmented optimal-control, and hierarchical reinforcement-learning baselines in efficiency and decision quality. The results support treating the design of the lower-level objective as a learnable part of a hierarchical architecture.
icml-2026-hierarchical-decision-making-w.tldr: The framework learns lower-level optimization structure from expert demonstrations to better align hierarchical decisions with long-term goals.

paragraphs: Robotic policies often generate chunks of actions to make behavior more consistent over time. At higher action frequencies, such as 60 Hz, chunking alone can become insufficient: actions may fail to remain smooth over time and consistent in space. This is especially consequential for contact-rich tasks, where pauses and jerky movements interrupt continuous execution.

The paper moves high-frequency action learning into a latent space built with a variational autoencoder. Learning in this representation significantly improves temporal and spatial consistency according to the authors. It also introduces Reuse-then-Refine, a strategy that refines action chunks to improve continuity between adjacent chunks when inference happens asynchronously. The two components address both action representation and the transitions between successive predictions.

Experiments on three real-world contact-rich robotic tasks show consistent task completion with smooth movements. Robots using the policy execute these tasks continuously with fewer pauses and jerks. The reported outcome connects smoother high-frequency control to two complementary choices: learning actions through a latent representation and explicitly managing continuity during real-time execution.
icml-2026-learning-high-frequency-contin.tldr: Latent-space action learning and Reuse-then-Refine improve smooth, continuous robot control across the three evaluated contact-rich tasks.

paragraphs: Tabular foundation models can compete with tree ensembles, but may use computation inefficiently. This paper identifies a bottleneck in standard scalar tokenization: changes in a feature’s value enter through essentially one direction. Feature identifiers and positional signals do not add independent ways to represent value variation within that feature, leaving early layers weakly sensitive to values and producing redundant hidden representations.

LimiX-2M changes both tokenization and information routing. RaBEL expands each scalar into compact, localized radial-basis features, optionally using exponent gating, to improve conditioning and effective rank in shallow layers. A reordered bidirectional block aggregates context across samples before mixing features and uses attention pooling. This ordering aligns internal computation more closely with how the model forms its final readout.

The resulting model has two million parameters. On widely used tabular benchmarks, it outperforms the larger TabPFN-v2 and TabICL baselines while reducing training and inference costs. The findings indicate that richer value representations and better ordering of information flow can improve accuracy and efficiency together in tabular foundation models.
icml-2026-limix-2m-mitigating-low-rank-c.tldr: LimiX-2M improves tabular prediction efficiency through richer scalar representations and readout-aligned attention routing.

paragraphs: Predicting where lipids bind to proteins is useful for biological research and therapeutic development. A central training problem is that an unrecorded interaction does not necessarily mean binding cannot occur. Models that label all unobserved cases as negatives therefore introduce systematic false negatives. LipoPU addresses this ambiguity while focusing on protein pockets, a less explored level than sequences or individual residues.

The method uses a ranking-based positive-unlabeled learning objective, distinguishing confirmed binding examples from cases with unknown status. It supports both deciding whether a pocket binds lipids and predicting multiple lipid categories. An attention-based pocket representation is designed to handle ambiguity in pocket definitions while exposing which residues contribute to the prediction.

Experiments report consistent improvements over supervised baselines and previous pocket-level methods. A structural case study also recovers an allosteric lipid-binding pocket supported by the literature and highlights biologically informative residues. These findings connect the treatment of uncertain labels with useful pocket-level predictions, while the residue-level interpretation helps explain what information the model uses.
icml-2026-lipopu-pocket-level-prediction.tldr: LipoPU predicts lipid-binding pockets using positive-unlabeled learning, avoiding the assumption that every unrecorded interaction is a negative example.

paragraphs: Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks offer a structured alternative to standard multilayer perceptrons, but their training and privacy properties have had limited theoretical grounding. This paper analyzes gradient descent for two-layer KANs, deriving bounds on optimization, generalization, and the utility retained when training satisfies differential privacy. The analysis connects model width, training duration, sample size, and privacy requirements.

For logistic loss under an NTK-separability assumption, the authors show that polylogarithmic width is sufficient for an optimization rate of order 1/T and a generalization rate of order 1/n. Here, T counts gradient-descent iterations and n counts samples. These are conditional results for the stated setting, rather than unrestricted guarantees for every KAN training problem.

For private training, the paper characterizes the required noise and obtains a utility bound of order square root of d divided by nε, matching a classical lower bound for general convex Lipschitz problems. Within the analysis, polylogarithmic width also becomes necessary under privacy, whereas non-private training establishes sufficiency only. Experiments illustrate how the theory can inform width selection and early stopping.
icml-2026-optimization-generalization-an.tldr: The paper derives conditional training, generalization, and privacy bounds for two-layer KANs, revealing different width requirements under private training.

paragraphs: Retrosynthesis predicts starting materials for a target molecule. Template-free generation can leave chemical structure implicit, while methods using reaction libraries face restrictions from those libraries. This paper introduces chemical structure through atom ordering: placing reaction-center atoms first gives the model an explicit positional pattern for the regions most important to the transformation.

The RetroDiT graph transformer uses rotary position embeddings to exploit this ordering. Combined with discrete flow matching, the framework separates training from sampling and generates in 20–50 steps, compared with 500 for the prior diffusion methods cited. The approach therefore uses a structural bias to guide learning while also reducing the number of generation steps.

With predicted reaction centers, the method reports leading top-1 results of 61.2% on USPTO-50k and 51.3% on USPTO-Full. With oracle centers, these rise to 71.1% and 63.4%; the reported advantage over foundation models trained on ten billion reactions applies to this oracle-center setting. An ablation further shows a 280K-parameter model with proper ordering matching a 65M-parameter model without it, demonstrating the value of ordering in that comparison.
icml-2026-order-matters-in-retrosynthesi.tldr: Reaction-center-first atom ordering helps RetroDiT improve retrosynthesis accuracy while discrete flow matching reduces generation steps.

paragraphs: Molecular property prediction often has to work with few labeled examples because obtaining reliable labels is expensive. Context-aware methods try to compensate by learning from related information, but that context can be poorly organized or contain redundant auxiliary signals. ReCoG addresses both problems: extracting useful relationships and limiting information that distracts from the prediction task.

Its cross-property relational learning module models structural and relational context more fully. A separate context-graph information bottleneck adaptively suppresses irrelevant auxiliary signals. These modules serve complementary purposes. Richer relational modeling expands what the representation can learn from the context graph, while compression concentrates that information on what is relevant to molecular property prediction.

The paper also provides a theoretical discussion of why relational and compact knowledge extraction should be considered jointly. Its stated contribution is a framework for making context more expressive without allowing auxiliary information to remain indiscriminately influential. For few-shot prediction, this matters because the method aims to use scarce supervision more effectively through better organized and more selective contextual learning.
icml-2026-recog-relational-and-compact-c.tldr: ReCoG combines cross-property relational learning with an information bottleneck to make molecular context more useful for few-shot prediction.

paragraphs: Decomposing a natural image into layers requires more than identifying visible objects. A system must separate overlapping content, recover hidden regions, and produce precise boundaries. RevealLayer tackles these challenges with a diffusion framework that converts an RGB image into multiple RGBA layers, where each layer includes both color and an alpha channel describing transparency.

Three components address different parts of the decomposition problem. Region-aware attention separates hidden and visible layers. An occlusion-guided adapter uses surrounding context to improve overlapping regions. A composite training loss encourages sharp alpha boundaries and reduces residual artifacts. Together, these mechanisms aim to make both the reconstructed content and its separation into layers more accurate.

The researchers also introduce RevealLayer-100K, a multilayer natural-image dataset assembled through automated processing and human annotation, and RevealLayerBench for evaluation in general natural scenes. Experiments report consistently better decomposition performance than existing approaches. The work combines modeling changes with new training and evaluation resources, addressing both image-understanding difficulties and the scarcity of suitable multilayer data.
icml-2026-reveallayer-disentangling-hidd.tldr: RevealLayer separates natural images into transparent layers using occlusion-aware diffusion components and introduces supporting data and benchmarks.

paragraphs: Amari alpha-divergences measure discrepancies between probability distributions and support variational inference. Estimating them with unconstrained neural critics can be unstable. This paper restricts the critic to a bounded reproducing kernel Hilbert space and approximates its kernel with band-limited random Fourier features. The resulting objective has linear-time complexity and supports minibatch optimization, avoiding cubic Gram-matrix computations.

The analysis separates error into approximation, feature discretization, statistical deviation, and unfinished optimization. Under a spectral source condition, approximation bias decreases as R to the power minus gamma, while feature and statistical errors scale as R divided by the square roots of feature count D and sample count n, respectively. These bounds expose a trade-off: increasing the critic radius R reduces approximation bias but enlarges other error terms.

The authors also show that statistical non-degeneracy supplies local curvature, enabling their Armijo-SGD method to converge linearly near a solution. Empirically, the estimator is more stable than the compared varying-representation baselines. Applying the same spectral regularization to GAN critics improves their capture of high-frequency data components.
icml-2026-scalable-and-stable-estimation.tldr: A bounded kernel critic approximated with random Fourier features enables scalable divergence estimation with conditional error and convergence guarantees.

paragraphs: Unsupervised domain adaptation for person search transfers a model from labeled source images to a target domain without target annotations. Camera height, tilt, focal length, and scene layout can change the scales at which people and their features appear. The paper argues that existing methods often overlook this mismatch, leaving an important source of transfer difficulty unresolved.

SCALE introduces a scale-aware harmonization module that aligns semantic and structural scales through interaction across processing paths and consistency refinement. It also addresses noisy pseudo-labels, the automatically inferred labels used when target annotations are unavailable. A bidirectional cluster regularization strategy performs a second, regularized clustering step to improve the reliability of those labels.

The method reports state-of-the-art results on two person-search benchmarks: 82.3% mAP and 84.0% top-1 on CUHK-SYSU, and 41.7% mAP and 82.4% top-1 on PRW. Its contribution is the coordinated treatment of scale mismatch and pseudo-label quality. The reported results indicate that improving both representation alignment and target supervision can strengthen transfer in this setting.
icml-2026-scale-aware-domain-harmonizati.tldr: SCALE improves person-search domain adaptation by aligning image scales and refining the pseudo-labels used for unlabeled target data.

paragraphs: Predicting trajectories of interacting bodies requires modeling both uncertainty and structured motion. Generative methods can represent distributions of possible trajectories, but their starting distributions often ignore relationships across time and spatial symmetries. The paper argues that this makes generation harder by requiring the model to transform a poorly matched prior into physically structured trajectory data.

GP-EquiFlow builds more suitable priors using vector-valued Gaussian processes conditioned on observed trajectories. These priors capture temporal relationships and are SE(3)-equivariant, meaning they respond consistently when the spatial coordinate system is rotated or translated. The flow-matching model therefore begins with a distribution that better agrees with the target trajectories’ spatial and temporal organization.

Experiments on N-body simulations and molecular dynamics show more accurate predictions with fewer sampling steps. The reported benefit comes from incorporating trajectory structure into the prior rather than leaving it entirely for the generative transformation to learn. These results support combining Gaussian-process temporal modeling with spatial equivariance when constructing starting distributions for geometric trajectory prediction.
icml-2026-se-3-equivariant-flow-matching.tldr: GP-EquiFlow uses temporally structured, spatially equivariant Gaussian-process priors to improve trajectory prediction with fewer sampling steps.

paragraphs: Compressing language-model weights to two bits can reduce deployment cost and accelerate inference, but the choice of representation creates trade-offs. Scalar quantization handles values individually and can lose substantial model quality at this precision. Vector quantization represents groups of values more flexibly, but brings additional computation and storage overhead. UniSVQ seeks a useful middle ground between these approaches.

The framework represents codewords through an affine transformation of integer lattices. This structured representation retains much of vector quantization’s flexibility while remaining compatible with optimized integer computation kernels. A data-driven, block-wise fine-tuning procedure directly minimizes reconstruction error caused by quantization, adapting the compressed representation to better preserve the model’s behavior.

Experiments across multiple language-model families and zero-shot benchmarks show consistently better performance than the compared state-of-the-art scalar methods. UniSVQ also achieves quality comparable to advanced vector methods while offering higher inference throughput. These findings suggest that carefully structured codewords can combine strong compression quality with efficient execution, reducing the practical tension between flexible representations and hardware-friendly arithmetic.
icml-2026-unisvq-2-bit-unified-scalar-ve.tldr: UniSVQ combines integer-compatible structure with vector-style flexibility to deliver accurate two-bit language-model compression and higher inference throughput.
